evidence.title: Maryland court rules Democratic-backed redistricting amendment cannot go on November ballot

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland Supreme Court appellate docket
occurrences.quote_span: Shortly after the ruling, the state filed a notice of appeal to the Maryland Supreme Court.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland governor's special-session proclamation and legislative records
occurrences.quote_span: Democratic Gov. Wes Moore called lawmakers into a special session in August with a goal of making it easier to claim that final seat.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland law and secretary of state's ballot-certification records
occurrences.quote_span: Earlier this year, lawmakers passed a law signed by Moore that set a July 1 deadline for the secretary of state to certify summaries of all statewide ballot questions to the Maryland State Board of Elections.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Robert Thompson's written ruling and Maryland legislative deadlines
occurrences.quote_span: Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson ruled that lawmakers violated their own deadlines for ballot measures.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement issued by Maryland House Speaker Joseline Peña-Melnyk
occurrences.quote_span: “We remain confident in the authority of the General Assembly and believe Maryland voters should have the final say,” she said in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Maryland House Speaker Joseline Peña-Melnyk
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland court ruling and documented state redistricting actions following President Trump's statements
occurrences.quote_span: The ruling Wednesday by a judge in the state's capital city marks another setback in Democrats' national attempts to counter a Republican redistricting movement pushed by President Donald Trump ahead of this year's elections.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Thompson's written ruling and Maryland Constitution
occurrences.quote_span: And Thompson said the amendment violates a single-issue requirement in the constitution by also including a provision that would give the state Supreme Court original jurisdiction in lawsuits over congressional redistricting.
occurrences.speaker: Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement issued by Marshall Yates or the Oversight Project
occurrences.quote_span: But “today's decision is a major step in our battle against Maryland’s lawless attempt at redistricting. Complete and total vindication!” Oversight Project Strategic Counsel Marshall Yates said in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Oversight Project Strategic Counsel Marshall Yates
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland court ruling on the proposed constitutional amendment
occurrences.quote_span: A Maryland court has ruled against a proposed constitutional amendment that could have paved the way for Democrats to redraw the state's congressional districts ahead of the 2028 elections.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Robert Thompson's ruling and Maryland Supreme Court docket
occurrences.quote_span: The judge ruled that the amendment cannot appear on the November ballot, but he paused the effect of that ruling to allow for an appeal to the state Supreme Court.
occurrences.speaker: Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Court filings by the Maryland attorney general's office
occurrences.quote_span: The state attorney general's office argued that deadline didn't apply to the redistricting amendment because lawmakers wrote their own ballot summary for it, using their constitutional authority.
occurrences.speaker: Maryland attorney general's office
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Proposed amendment text, Maryland congressional district map, and House membership records
occurrences.quote_span: That would allow Democratic state lawmakers to draw congressional districts that cross the Chesapeake Bay, reshaping a district east of the bay that is held by Republican Rep. Andy Harris, chair of the conservative House Freedom Caucus.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Text of the proposed Maryland constitutional amendment
occurrences.quote_span: It would declare that a constitutional requirement for districts to be compact and take into account “natural boundaries” applies only to state legislative districts, not congressional ones.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Current Maryland congressional delegation records
occurrences.quote_span: Democrats already control seven of Maryland's eight congressional seats.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Thompson's written ruling and court case filings by the Oversight Project and Republican Maryland lawmakers
occurrences.quote_span: The judge disagreed, instead siding with arguments by the conservative Oversight Project and Republican state lawmakers who sued.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Thompson's written ruling and Maryland ballot question text
occurrences.quote_span: Thompson also ruled that lawmakers used “intentionally misleading” wording in the ballot question by stating that it merely “clarifies” the constitution's redistricting standards.
occurrences.speaker: Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Maryland ballot referral records and 2022 court ruling
occurrences.quote_span: An amendment referred to the ballot by lawmakers seeks to sidestep a court ruling that struck down a previous Democratic redistricting plan in 2022.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment

occurrences.checkable_against: Judge Thompson's written injunction and Maryland State Board of Elections ballot records
occurrences.quote_span: “The court has no choice but to enjoin the board of elections from including ballot Question 3 on the general election ballot for November 3, 2026,” Thompson wrote.
occurrences.speaker: Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Judge Robert Thompson
occurrences.subject: Maryland redistricting amendment
